Subject: MAP: cost & unit-econ handoff / choke-points to validate

Emily —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we move into the formal MAP for the pilot, our team needs a tight set of cost and unit-economics checks so we can produce an accurate tokens-per-dollar projection for procurement and exec review. High level asks before our working session on Wednesday: 

- Typical daily/weekly traffic profile (peak qps, 95th pct window, percent conversational vs. single-shot)
- Example payload sizes (avg tokens in prompt + expected response tokens per interaction)
- Any hard latency SLOs we need to design for (p95 target, tail limits)
- Whether you expect to use prefix/cacheable content (document retrieval) vs. open generation in most flows

Im attaching a lightweight worksheet with the inputs we will use (Solace_MAP_econ_worksheet.xlsx) and a short sim of a prefetch/caching run we did against a similar traffic shape (prefetch_sim_results.pdf). During the MAP we'll validate: token assumptions, likely cache hit rates (we'll run quick prefix-hit sims), and batching/microbatching tradeoffs for your latency targets.

If procurement wants upfront numbers to ballpark a budget, call those "units/$" estimates — we'll provide a mid-case and conservative-case based on caching hit rates and microbatch size.

Proposed next step: 30-min sync Wednesday 07/14 at 10:00am PT to walk the worksheet and call out any redlines. Can you confirm attendees?

Thanks,
Laura

Emily / team —

Perfect, that profile helps. I've updated the worksheet with a mid / low / high traffic column and seeded the prompt/response token fields with your numbers. For tomorrow's call we'll validate three gating assumptions that typically swing units/$: 

1) Cacheability: If ~30-40% of requests can be served from a prefix/KV cache (FAQ lookup, canonical responses), that reduces token compute by roughly the cache hit fraction. We'll need a short sample of canonical prompts to run a hit-rate sweep.

2) Microbatch sizing vs tail latency: For p95 < 350ms, we expect to use microbatch sizes of 4-8 requests on our Dedicated profile; larger batches help throughput but can increase p95 in burst windows. We'll show a latency vs throughput curve.

3) Prefetch/warm-up windows: For heavier peaks (220 qps spikes) we recommend a short prefetch/KV warm-up and reserved concurrency to avoid cold-start tail penalties.

Attachments: Solace_MAP_econ_worksheet.xlsx (seeded inputs) and prefetch_sim_results.pdf (our prefetched-sim run against a comparable healthcare workload).

If Karthik / Ben / Tessa have last-minute checks, please flag them now. Otherwise we'll walk the worksheet and propose the two price points for procurement (pilot estimate + committed run-rate).

See you tomorrow — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-14T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: cost & unit-econ handoff / choke-points to validate

Laura / team —

Quick internal notes from our prep: 

- For Solace's traffic shape (avg 80 qps, spikes to 220) we should prepare two model variants: quantized medium for default (cheaper) and an nbit-high-quality variant for degraded fallbacks. Routing policy: prefer quantized unless p95 threshold violated.

- EV (expected value) calc idea: mid-case cache hit 25% (they said many single-shot but 18% multi-turn). We'll produce tokens/$ for hit rates 10/25/40%.

- Prefetch sim: in our prefetch_sim_results we saw a 22% token reduction with a conservative prefix-match threshold (sim uses 0.88 embedding-sim cutoff). We should surface embedding threshold sensitivity in the MAP; it's a major lever.

- Batching: propose microbatch=6 for steady state; autoscale concurrency to hold p95 < 350ms during spikes (canary with 25% extra capacity during initial pilot).

I'll turn these into a short runbook blurb to drop into the MAP steps, and add a HubSpot note with the cost table. Drive link below for the working worksheet.

Karthik
